subject: RetailCorp latency spike — RCA deliverable & exec action roster
messages:
From: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@retailcorp.com>, procurement@retailcorp.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:22:00 +0000
Subject: High latency & 5xx affecting checkout — urgent

Jasmine / Redwood team,

We started seeing a latency spike and a rise in 5xx errors on our checkout flows beginning ~14:58 UTC. Latency climbed from our usual ~180ms to >1200ms for a subset of requests, and overall error rate hit 3.8% for ~20 minutes. This impacted several checkout sessions and caused order processing delays.

Attached is a short error sample (error-sample.txt) and a couple of screenshots from our monitoring dashboard. We need immediate triage and an exec-level readout — leadership is asking for the root cause, impact window, and steps to ensure this doesn't recur.

Please confirm receipt and what you need from us.

Thanks,
Dana Ortiz
Head of Engineering, RetailCorp
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 15:34:12 +0000
Subject: Re: High latency & 5xx affecting checkout — urgent

Dana — thank you for the heads up and the samples. We’ve opened an incident and are standing up an ad-hoc bridge.

Immediate actions: 
- 15:35 UTC: we started ingesting your error-sample and traces
- 15:37 UTC: spare team on a bridge (incl. Karthik and Markus)
- Can you confirm if you changed traffic routing, feature flags, or increased concurrency from a marketing push around 14:45–15:00 UTC?

We’ll send a concise incident summary within the hour and follow up with a proposed RCA timeline. Apologies for the disruption — we’re on it.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:05:47 +0000
Subject: Incident triage notes — initial findings

Team, quick triage notes from the bridge (summary):
- Impact window: ~14:58–15:20 UTC. Peak at ~15:03 UTC.
- Symptom: elevated tail latency and ~3–4% 5xx spike tied to specific API route /v1/checkout/complete.
- Initial signal: heavy prefix variance in requests (longer variable user metadata) causing KV cache churn on the serving nodes.
- Observed behavior: several requests dropped to a slower kernel execution path (fallback path) once KV cache hit ratio dropped below threshold. Those slower paths increased per-token processing time and pushed queueing, which raised upstream error rates.

Action items we raised on the bridge:
1) Gather full timeline and request-level traces — Markus (owner) — due 2027-05-26
2) Produce draft RCA describing cache churn mechanics and kernel fallback — Markus & Karthik — due 2027-06-01
3) Temporary mitigation: enable stricter prefix trimming + scale up burst capacity for RetailCorp Dedicated pool — Jasmine (owner for comms) & Ops — ASAP

I’ll attach the trace ids and a compact timeline when ready.

On the bridge we also requested impact quantification (orders affected) from RetailCorp.

-Karthik
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:02:00 +0000
Subject: RetailCorp RCA + corrective actions (draft)

Dana / Jasmine — attaching the RCA packet (RetailCorp_latency_RCA_v1.pdf) and a machine timeline (timeline.csv). Highlights below: 

Root cause (short): an unexpected traffic pattern introduced large prefix variance across requests; this reduced KV cache locality on retired-serving nodes and caused high KV eviction churn. The serving runtime, observing low cache hit ratios, selected a safe but slower kernel/quantization execution path for affected model variants. That swap increased per-token latency by ~6–8x for the hot path and caused queueing and 5xx propagation at the API layer.

Contributing factors:
- No prefix-normalization at the routing layer for this route (we relied on application-side trimming).
- Burst autoscale policy conservatively delayed GPU spin-up for short surges.
- Model-variant selection logic fell back to a fully-accurate execution kernel rather than an intermediate fast path when KV cache below threshold.

Immediate mitigations applied (2027-05-24 post-incident):
- Enabled prefix trimming rule at the routing layer for /v1/checkout/* (reduced variance) — deployed 15:45 UTC.
- Temporarily bumped burst capacity and reduced autoscale cooldown — rolled 16:10 UTC.
- Added a per-customer model-variant pin for RetailCorp to avoid cross-tenant variant churn — rolled 16:35 UTC.

Recommended corrective actions (owners & deadlines):
A) Persistent prefix normalization at ingress (Product & Runtime) — Owner: Markus Klein — target 2027-06-09
B) Autoscale profile update (Ops) to allow faster burst GPU provisioning for Reserved pools — Owner: Grace O'Connor — target 2027-06-04
C) Kernel selection policy refinement to prefer intermediate fast paths during transient low-hit windows — Owner: Runtime Eng — Owner contact: runtime-eng@redwood.ai — target 2027-06-16
D) Post-implementation load test and verification with RetailCorp test harness — Owner: Jasmine Liu + RetailCorp Eng — target 2027-06-18

Attached: RetailCorp_latency_RCA_v1.pdf (full write-up), timeline.csv (request-level timestamps and trace-ids).

Please review and let us know if you want a recorded exec readout.

— Markus Klein
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:12:08 +0000
Subject: Executive note & service credit offer

Dana — I’ve reviewed Markus’ RCA and the mitigation timeline. We own the customer impact and want to move from reactive to preventive measures.

As a commitment while we complete the recommended fixes, we are offering RetailCorp a goodwill service credit equivalent to 1 month of committed Reserved capacity usage (terms attached). We will also provide a snapshot of audit logs and request traces for the impacted window.

Next steps we propose:
- 2027-06-04: Ops autoscale profile update complete (Grace)
- 2027-06-09: Prefix normalization deployed (Markus)
- 2027-06-18: Joint verification load test (Jasmine + RetailCorp)

If that cadence works for you, we’ll prepare a short exec readout (15–20 min) the week after the autoscale update. Term sheet attached: service-credit-term-sheet.pdf.

Sincerely,
Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@retailcorp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@retailcorp.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 23:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Executive note & service credit offer

Thanks, Grace and team. We reviewed Markus’ RCA and the attachments. The proposed fixes and dates look reasonable. We accept the goodwill credit and would like the joint verification load test scheduled for 2027-06-18 — please confirm an exact window and test profile.

Also please include the audit logs for 2027-05-24 14:45–15:30 UTC in the shared drive link so our SREs can reconcile traces.

Appreciate the prompt handling and the clear action owners. Once we have the verification run and audit logs we’ll mark the incident closed on our side.

— Dana Ortiz
Head of Engineering, RetailCorp
